title: Lift Equation Explorer
learningObjectives: Calculate lift from lift coefficient, air density, velocity, and wing area using the lift equation
Explain how lift depends on density, velocity squared, wing area, and lift coefficient
Describe dynamic pressure as density times velocity squared divided by two

evidence.quote: lift L is equal to the lift coefficient Cl times the density rho

explanations.text: Lift equals the lift coefficient times dynamic pressure times wing area. Doubling wing area doubles lift, while doubling velocity quadruples lift.

evidence.quote: For lift, this variable is called the lift coefficient, designated "Cl."
This allows us to collect all the effects, simple and complex, into a single equation.

explanations.text: The lift coefficient collects complex shape, inclination, viscosity, and compressibility effects into a single variable used to calculate lift.

evidence.quote: "density times the square of the velocity divided by two" is called the dynamic pressure

explanations.text: Dynamic pressure is density times velocity squared divided by two. Higher density or higher velocity increases dynamic pressure and therefore lift.
